header:
Problem 7 Reactivity, Preparation, and Applications of Silanes (32 points, 10%)
Silanes ($Si_nH_{2n+2}$) and their halogenated derivatives are important precursors for high-purity silicon films, semiconductor devices, and solar cells. Unlike hydrocarbons, silanes contain highly reactive Si–Si and Si–H bonds, creating distinctive challenges in their synthesis and purification.

subquestions.text_open:
7.4.3 Mixing the tridentate ligand pedeta (pentaethyldiethylenetriamine, $Et_2NCH_2CH_2NEtCH_2CH_2NEt_2$) with trichlorosilane in DCM at room temperature gives A = $[(pedeta)H_2SiCl^+]_2[Si_6Cl_{14}^{2-}]$.
7.4.3.1 How many stereoisomers can the cation of A theoretically have?
7.4.3.2 The anion of A has an approximate sixfold rotation axis. Write its SMILES string.

7.4.3.3 Mechanistic experiments show that adding 1,3-butadiene to this reaction system does not produce detectable 1,1-dichlorosilacyclopent-3-ene. Which of the following is therefore the most likely key one-silicon intermediate?
A. $:SiCl_2$
B. $SiCl_3$
C. $SiCl_3^-$
D. $SiCl_4^-$

7.5 Wurtz coupling. More complex silane molecules can be obtained through Wurtz coupling.
7.5.1 Mechanistically, which class does the first reaction belong to?
A. Nucleophilic aromatic substitution
B. Electrophilic aromatic substitution
C. Radical substitution
D. Transition-metal-catalyzed reaction
